messages:
Sam: Hey folks — pinging for quick eyes on PR #8355 (alloc scheduler tweak). Canary showed allocator oscillation + a small p95 tail bump on longseq workloads. bench artifacts: https://bench.redwood/8355/artifacts :eyes:

Sam: Key summary: after the alloc-window change we see transient mem spikes and p95 +18% for 4k seq on canary; throughput roughly flat. I attached a short heap trace and the microbench CSV.

Sam: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T21:12:03Z] worker-7: alloc_queue_size=312 -> 28 -> 305 (oscillation)
[2026-03-17T21:12:05Z] mem_rss_mb: 12345 -> 13780 -> 12510
```

Maya: ack, looking. Do we have the exact commit diff that changed the pacing? link?

Sam: yes — https://git.redwood/pr/8355/commits/7b9c2a ; offending change is the new backpressure window adjustment (line ~212).

Leo: quick thought: hold the mainline canary. Recommend phased canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Rollback triggers: p95 > baseline * 1.1 OR any OOMs or alloc oscillation > 3 cycles in 10m.

Ana: +1 on a phased plan. Also please add a concise perf-regression note to PR body with links to artifacts and the hypothesis (alloc pacing). Tagging reviewers: @Maya, @Leo, @Jules for perf/alloc.

Jules: ran a quick local microbench (same model + 4k seq): baseline p95=84ms, PR p95=99ms. Throughput (tokens/s) baseline 4200 -> PR 4150. So small tail increase but not catastrophic. Full CSV uploaded to artifacts.

InfraBot: Artifact upload complete: https://bench.redwood/8355/artifacts/summary.csv | Benchmark-run-id=run-20260317-2130

Sam: thanks — I'll update PR with the phased canary and the explicit rollback thresholds. Can I get quick approves from @Maya and @Leo when you have a minute?

Maya: I'll review and try to approve by EOD. :thumbsup:

Leo: I'll do a quick pass — if nothing else urgent I'll approve and coordinate the 5% -> 25% rollout in the canary job.

Sam: great. I'll also add a perf smoke test in the canary job to auto-fail on p95 > baseline*1.1 so we don't make the mistake of blindly promoting.

Ana: add the SLO exception ticket if we need to keep the canary longer than the usual window.

Sam: will do. Thanks all — updating now. :pray:
